messages:
Alicia: Heads up — ran a control microbench comparing kernel-selector v2.1 against v2 under our replay harness. Variables: replay traces (prod-1), kv-cache warm/unwarm, quant=int8/fp16, spec-decoding on/off. Seeing ~15% p50 regression when kv-cache is cold + int8. Anyone else seeing this?

Kevin: Can you paste the harness command you ran?

Alicia: Sure, command I used:

```
./tools/run_microbench \
  --harness=replay \
  --trace=prod-1.trace \
  --kernels=v2,v2.1 \
  --quantizations=int8,fp16 \
  --kv_warm=true,false \
  --speculative=true,false \
  --runs=1500 \
  --collect-trace=nvprof
```

PerfBot: perfbot: job=bench-1864501234 finished. summary: p50(v2,fp16,cold-kv)=68ms, p50(v2.1,int8,cold-kv)=78ms (+14.7%). p95 tail also up ~22%. Artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/bench-1864501234/

Sandeep: That gap is suspiciously kernel-level. I remember a selector tweak in v2.1 that prefers the new fused-mm kernel only for batch_size>=4 and seq_len<=128. For many of these replay requests batch=1, seq around 96, so maybe it picked a slower fallback for int8.

Jasper: Do we have nvprof/cupti flame samples? Any extra memcpy or syncs?

Alicia: Quick nvprof snippet from the cold-kv+int8 run (filtered):

```
KernelName           Calls  TotalTime(ms)
--------------------------------------
fused_mm_v2.1         1      40.3
matmul_fp16           2      12.1
gather_kv             6      10.2
memcpy_h2d            3      5.8
sync_device           1      3.9
```

Alicia: So fused_mm_v2.1 is heavy but we thought it would be faster. Profiling shows higher SM stalls and more syncs in the int8 path.

Kevin: Could be that quant codepath triggers a different kernel launch configuration (more warps, smaller occupancy). The selector might be scoring kernels by throughput ignoring warm vs cold KV. Our batching heuristic also routes many short seq singletons to the quantized lane to save cost. That could hurt latency.

Sandeep: Agreed. Two short-term actions: 1) gate the selector tweak behind regression flag and revert on canary; 2) run an apples-to-apples replay canary where only selector changes, keep batching and quantization config identical.

Alicia: I'll run the canary revert. Repro steps I'm going to use:

```
export REG_GATE=selector_v2.1_revert
./deploy_canary.sh --shard=us-west-2 --tag=bench-canary-186450 \
  && ./tools/run_microbench --harness=replay --trace=prod-1.trace --kernels=v2 --quantizations=int8 --kv_warm=false --runs=5000
```

PerfBot: perfbot: canary deployed to shard-us-west-2. starting 5k replay requests (bench-canary-186450). logs: /logs/canary-186450/

Jasper: Also include speculative-decoding=true/false in the matrix. Speculative can mask single-token latency but changes token emission patterns; good to know if it affects tail.

Alicia: Will run full matrix: selector x quant x speculative x kv_warm. Expecting to produce a heatmap and p50/p90/p95/tail.

Kevin: Add token-quality eval (bleu/rouge or loss on eval prompts) to ensure int8+spec don't regress output. Also record token emission distribution for speculative.

Sandeep: If the regression is strictly cold-kv, we should consider: a) tweak KV prefetch to warm on first prefix, b) adjust the selector to prefer kernels with better cold-cache behavior, or c) add a lightweight early-warm probe in routing.

Alicia: Good ideas. I'll collect traces and profiler outputs and open a PR with the failing harness + artifacts. Will also attach the NVTX timeline.

Kevin: Thanks. Once you have canary numbers, tag me and I'll help with the kernel scoring change. :thumbsup: 

Alicia: Thanks all — filing follow-up thread with artifacts and heatmaps. :eyes:
